segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics news digest for September 7th, 2026.
We've got updates on new ROS tools, exciting NASA challenges, and tips for learning ROS 2.
Tune in for the latest!
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: New CLI tool: fastdds_transport_viz — predict & measure per-topic DDS transport in ROS 2".
This report details the introduction of a new Command Line Interface tool designed to predict and measure the DDS transport utilized by ROS 2 topics.
The tool determines the transport mechanism, including UDPv4/v6, TCP, SHM, or zero-copy data-sharing, for each topic based on Fast DDS discovery data.
It measures real traffic statistics, including rate and latency, by utilizing the Fast DDS statistics module.
The tool provides various output options such as a live view, JSON output, and a web viewer, and has been verified across different ROS 2 distributions and hardware setups.
This advancement offers deeper insight into the underlying communication infrastructure of ROS 2 systems.
Further analysis of this transport data will inform optimization strategies for real-time systems development.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: NASA Space Roboticist Challenge: propose an experiment for a 7-DoF arm in orbit (U.S.; registration closes Sep 23)".
This segment details an opportunity for U.S. researchers to propose experiments utilizing a seven degrees of freedom robotic arm in low Earth orbit as part of the Space Roboticist Challenge.
The process requires submitting a white paper outlining a focused experiment, followed by a simulation and validation phase with NASA engineers before potential on-orbit execution.
Eligibility is limited to U.S. citizens and permanent residents affiliated with eligible U.S. institutions possessing faculty sponsorship.
Registration for this challenge closes on September 23, 2026, with white paper submissions due in October 2026.
This initiative provides a structured pathway for applying advanced robotic experimentation in the space environment.
The results will inform future methodologies for in-orbit manipulation and remote system interaction in microgravity.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: What is the hardest part of learning ROS 2 as a beginner"
addresses the primary difficulties encountered by newcomers in learning the Robot Operating System 2 framework.
The report highlights that beginners frequently experience challenges related to workspace setup and sourcing procedures before writing actual robot code.

The content documented the entire process, including error handling, detailing the steps for workspace configuration, package management, establishing the initial node, understanding entry points, and the requirement for per-terminal sourcing.
A central difficulty identified is the conceptual understanding of why sourcing is mandatory for each separate terminal session during the workflow.
This information is specifically tailored for absolute first-week beginners to resolve initial setup obstacles.
This insight clarifies the foundational procedural hurdles in adopting ROS 2 environments for new developers.
And that's all the circuits for today!
Hope your day runs as smoothly as a perfectly tuned DDS transport.
Until tomorrow, keep those bots building!
Bye for now.
